A1.justification: Despite the changed title and extensive reorganization, both PDFs describe the same sampled RNN and Koopman framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original forecasting, control and training-time results on synthetic systems, weather, electricity consumption and bike traffic, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original forecasting and control results and reports additional crowd-density experiments and real-data baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: KIRNN retains the sampled RNN's data-dependent sampling, EDMD fitting, state projection and LQR control. Nonlinear control-input lifting was already described and tested in v2 Appendix H.1.1; v3 formalizes this existing variant and uses it in the main control experiment.

E1.justification: v3 Section 3.5 adds pedestrian-bottleneck crowd-density modeling, while the Copenhagen bike-count experiment in v2 Appendix I disappears. Electricity consumption moves into the main text and remains existing coverage. The oscillator, chaotic-system and weather tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The real-data comparisons change substantially: ESN replaces LSTM in both weather-horizon comparisons, and ESN and shPLRNN are added against the previously standalone electricity model. ESN and shPLRNN remain the synthetic-system comparators; citing crowd-modeling work does not constitute another evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Reported weather shPLRNN settings change from 200 to 300 hidden dimensions, sequence length 40 to 100, and 2500 to 1000 epochs. Electricity-model width changes from 128 to 64. The main control experiment replaces identity input lifting with a 32-node nonlinear layer. The crowd experiment introduces its own preprocessing and model configuration.

E4.justification: v3 adds crowd-mode and eigenvalue-residual analysis but removes v2's Van der Pol neuron-coverage visualization, training-time scaling, chaotic-system width ablations, and time-step sensitivity study. Component ablations remain for Van der Pol, while the Lorenz/Rössler component results disappear. The Van der Pol training-versus-validation width analysis is retained as Figure 11.

E5.justification: Five varying-seed runs with mean/minimum/maximum reporting remain the general practice. v3 additionally supplies explicit ranges for controller cost and electricity results, which v2 reported as scalar values. This extends uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: Synthetic benchmark values in Table 1 remain unchanged, but new crowd and electricity-baseline results appear. Weekly-weather shPLRNN error changes from 2.604 to 5.412, controller cost from 125.92 to 13.96, and the proposed electricity model's test error from 1.428 to 1.66. These accompany revised configurations and do not establish same-setting performance changes. Bike and several supplementary results disappear.

T1.justification: The convergence theorem and underlying proof are largely retained despite renumbering. v3 adds explicit quadratic-cost, Riccati and feedback equations in Section 2.3, corrects the printed Van der Pol equation, and restores a squared-norm term in the Appendix B proof.

C1.justification: The central gradient-free construction claim remains. The abstract narrows alleviating all backpropagation problems to some problems, and replaces improved forecasting accuracy with comparable accuracy alongside faster training. These are limited but substantive qualifications of the original claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive manifold-based explanation for repeatedly projecting and lifting states, clarifies the requirement for explicitly constructed observable states, and identifies gaps concerning ReLU and random-sampling guarantees. It also interprets crowd modes and residuals, and explicitly limits the control demonstration pending comparisons with nonlinear-control methods.

D1.justification: v3 adds crowd preprocessing details, electricity and ESN tuning settings, and previously unstated shPLRNN layer counts. LSTM implementation details and the teacher-forcing-interval table row disappear. Reported code locations change from the swimrnn repositories to kirnn repositories; actual availability was not externally checked.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around dynamical-system RNNs, nonlinear control, pedestrian dynamics and spectral verification, including Kern et al., Colbrook and Townsend, and Lazar. It explicitly presents KIRNN as a possible reservoir architecture, while removing much of v2's broader loss-function and interpretability survey. Publication updates to retained references are not new works.

P1.justification: The title and method terminology change, the introduction and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten, and mathematical explanations expand substantially. Baseline descriptions and dataset details move from appendices into the main text. Appendices A–J are consolidated into A–D, and the separate ethics and reproducibility sections disappear.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn as a simpler lifting–evolution–projection diagram. New crowd-density and spectral displays appear; control and weather displays change; weather and electricity split plots are combined. Numerous appendix plots disappear, and comparison tables, hyperparameter tables and algorithm layouts are extensively reorganized.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies applicability, tempers accuracy claims, and adds useful crowd-mode analysis and electricity comparisons. However, it removes evidence about chaotic-system ablations and time-step robustness. Its weather discussion contradicts Table 1, and Section 2.3 applies a lifted-space feedback gain directly to the original state without reconciling dimensions. These substantive benefits and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
